import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Kusner conjecture

A set $S$ of points of a metric space is *equilateral* (its points are *equidistant*) if there is
some $\lambda > 0$ such that any two distinct points of $S$ are at distance exactly $\lambda$.
The *equilateral dimension* of a metric space is the maximum size of an equilateral set in it.

Let $\ell_1^d$ denote $\mathbb{R}^d$ with the $L^1$ (Manhattan) norm
$\|x\|_1 = |x_1| + \cdots + |x_d|$. The $2d$ vertices $\pm e_i$ of the axis-aligned cross-polytope
are pairwise at $L^1$-distance $2$, so the equilateral dimension of $\ell_1^d$ is at least $2d$.
Kusner's conjecture (1983) states that this is sharp: at most $2d$ points of $\ell_1^d$ can be
equidistant, i.e. the equilateral dimension of $\ell_1^d$ is exactly $2d$. The conjecture is known
for $d \le 4$, and the equilateral dimension of $\ell_1^d$ is $O(d \log d)$ in general.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Kusner conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kusner_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Guy83] Guy, R. K., *An olla-podrida of open problems, often oddly posed*,
  Amer. Math. Monthly 90 (1983), 196–200.
- [KLS00] Koolen, J., Laurent, M. and Schrijver, A., *Equilateral dimension of the rectilinear
  space*, Des. Codes Cryptogr. 21 (2000), 149–164.
- [AP03] Alon, N. and Pudlák, P., *Equilateral sets in $l_p^n$*, Geom. Funct. Anal. 13 (2003),
  467–482.
- [Sw04] Swanepoel, K. J., *A problem of Kusner on equilateral sets*, Arch. Math. 83 (2004),
  164–170. [arXiv:math/0309317](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0309317)
-/

open WithLp

namespace KusnerConjecture

/-- The space $\ell_1^d$: $\mathbb{R}^d$ equipped with the $L^1$ (Manhattan) norm
$\|x\|_1 = \sum_{i} |x_i|$. -/
local notation "ℓ¹[" d "]" => PiLp 1 (fun _ : Fin d => ℝ)

/-- A set `S` in a (pseudo)metric space is *equilateral*, i.e. its points are *equidistant*, if
there is a positive real `r` such that any two distinct points of `S` are at distance exactly
`r`. -/
def IsEquilateral {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X] (S : Set X) : Prop :=
  ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ ∀ x ∈ S, ∀ y ∈ S, x ≠ y → dist x y = r

@[category test, AMS 51]
theorem isEquilateral_empty {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X] : IsEquilateral (∅ : Set X) :=
  ⟨1, one_pos, by simp⟩

@[category test, AMS 51]
theorem isEquilateral_singleton {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X] (x : X) :
    IsEquilateral {x} :=
  ⟨1, one_pos, by simp⟩

@[category test, AMS 51]
theorem isEquilateral_pair {X : Type*} [MetricSpace X] {x y : X} (h : x ≠ y) :
    IsEquilateral {x, y} :=
  ⟨dist x y, dist_pos.2 h, by aesop (add norm dist_comm)⟩

/-- In $\ell_1^1 = \mathbb{R}$, the three points $0, 1, 3$ are not equidistant. -/
@[category test, AMS 51]
theorem not_isEquilateral_example :
    ¬ IsEquilateral ({toLp 1 ![0], toLp 1 ![1], toLp 1 ![3]} : Set ℓ¹[1]) := by
  rintro ⟨r, -, hr⟩
  have h₁ := hr (toLp 1 ![0]) (by simp) (toLp 1 ![1]) (by simp) (by simp)
  have h₂ := hr (toLp 1 ![0]) (by simp) (toLp 1 ![3]) (by simp) (by simp)
  simp [PiLp.dist_eq_of_L1] at h₁ h₂
  linarith

/-- The $L^1$-distance between $a e_i$ and $b e_j$ is $|a| + |b|$ when $i \ne j$. -/
@[category API, AMS 51]
theorem dist_single_single_of_ne {d : ℕ} {i j : Fin d} (hij : i ≠ j) (a b : ℝ) :
    dist (toLp 1 (Pi.single i a) : ℓ¹[d]) (toLp 1 (Pi.single j b)) = |a| + |b| := by
  rw [PiLp.dist_eq_of_L1]
  have h : ∀ k, dist ((Pi.single i a : Fin d → ℝ) k) ((Pi.single j b : Fin d → ℝ) k) =
      (Pi.single i |a| : Fin d → ℝ) k + (Pi.single j |b| : Fin d → ℝ) k := by
    intro k
    rcases eq_or_ne k i with rfl | hki
    · simp [hij.symm]
    · rcases eq_or_ne k j with rfl | hkj
      · simp [hki]
      · simp [hki, hkj]
  simp [h, Finset.sum_add_distrib]

/-- The vertices $\pm e_i$ of the axis-aligned cross-polytope in $\ell_1^d$. -/
def crossPolytopeVertices (d : ℕ) : Set ℓ¹[d] :=
  Set.range (fun i : Fin d => toLp 1 (Pi.single i 1)) ∪
    Set.range (fun i : Fin d => toLp 1 (Pi.single i (-1)))

/-- The vertices of the cross-polytope are pairwise at $L^1$-distance $2$, so they form an
equilateral set in $\ell_1^d$. -/
@[category test, AMS 51 52]
theorem isEquilateral_crossPolytopeVertices (d : ℕ) :
    IsEquilateral (crossPolytopeVertices d) := by
  refine ⟨2, two_pos, ?_⟩
  rintro x (⟨i, rfl⟩ | ⟨i, rfl⟩) y (⟨j, rfl⟩ | ⟨j, rfl⟩) hxy <;>
    rcases eq_or_ne i j with rfl | hij <;>
    simp_all [dist_single_single_of_ne, Real.dist_eq] <;> norm_num

/-- The cross-polytope in $\ell_1^d$ has exactly $2d$ vertices. -/
@[category API, AMS 51 52]
theorem encard_crossPolytopeVertices (d : ℕ) : (crossPolytopeVertices d).encard = 2 * d := by
  have hinj : ∀ a : ℝ, a ≠ 0 →
      Function.Injective (fun i : Fin d => (toLp 1 (Pi.single i a) : ℓ¹[d])) := by
    intro a ha i j hij
    have := congrFun (congrArg ofLp hij) i
    by_contra h
    simp [h, ha] at this
  have hdisj : Disjoint (Set.range (fun i : Fin d => (toLp 1 (Pi.single i 1) : ℓ¹[d])))
      (Set.range (fun i : Fin d => toLp 1 (Pi.single i (-1)))) := by
    rw [Set.disjoint_left]
    rintro x ⟨i, rfl⟩ ⟨j, hj⟩
    have := congrFun (congrArg ofLp hj) i
    rcases eq_or_ne i j with rfl | hij
    · norm_num at this
    · simp [hij.symm] at this
  rw [crossPolytopeVertices, Set.encard_union_eq hdisj, ← Set.image_univ,
    (hinj 1 one_ne_zero).encard_image, ← Set.image_univ, (hinj (-1) (by norm_num)).encard_image]
  simp [two_mul]

/-- The equilateral dimension of $\ell_1^d$ is at least $2d$: the $2d$ vertices $\pm e_i$ of the
cross-polytope are equidistant. This is the easy half of the equality conjectured by Kusner. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 46 51 52]
theorem exists_isEquilateral_encard_eq (d : ℕ) :
    ∃ S : Set ℓ¹[d], IsEquilateral S ∧ S.encard = 2 * d :=
  ⟨crossPolytopeVertices d, isEquilateral_crossPolytopeVertices d, encard_crossPolytopeVertices d⟩

/-- **Kusner's conjecture.** For every $d \ge 1$, at most $2d$ points can be equidistant in
$\ell_1^d$: any set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ whose distinct points are all at the same
(positive) $L^1$-distance from each other satisfies $|S| \le 2d$. Together with
`exists_isEquilateral_encard_eq`, this says that the equilateral dimension of $\ell_1^d$ is
exactly $2d$.

The restriction $d \ge 1$ excludes the degenerate case $d = 0$, where $\ell_1^0$ is a single
point and so has a (vacuously) equidistant set of $1 > 2 \cdot 0$ points. -/
@[category research open, AMS 46 51 52]
theorem kusner_conjecture (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) (S : Set ℓ¹[d]) (hS : IsEquilateral S) :
    S.encard ≤ 2 * d := by
  sorry

end KusnerConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single slot (upper bound 2d for equilateral sets in ℓ¹_d, d ≥ 1) is the correct reading of the list entry; the d ≥ 1 restriction in the notes is indeed required for the statement to be true.
modeling_decisions: The terse list entry 'at most 2d points can be equidistant in L¹ spaces' is read, following the Wikipedia 'Equilateral dimension' article and Swanepoel's definition, as: for every d ≥ 1, every equilateral set in ℓ¹_d = (ℝ^d, ‖·‖₁) has at most 2d points (i.e. the equilateral dimension of ℓ¹_d is ≤ 2d).

ℓ¹_d is modelled as Mathlib's `PiLp 1 (fun _ : Fin d => ℝ)` (via a local notation ℓ¹[d]); its metric is the Manhattan distance ∑ᵢ |xᵢ − yᵢ| (`PiLp.dist_eq_of_L1`). The test `isEquilateral_crossPolytopeVertices` (±eᵢ pairwise at distance 2) only holds for the ℓ¹ metric, so it validates the choice of space.

Equilateral set: `IsEquilateral S := ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ ∀ x ∈ S, ∀ y ∈ S, x ≠ y → dist x y = r`, matching the literature's 'λ-equilateral for some λ > 0'. In a metric space the positivity of r is automatic when S has ≥ 2 points and irrelevant otherwise, so it does not change the claim.

Cardinality is expressed with `Set.encard ≤ 2 * d` on arbitrary sets (not Finset), so infinite equidistant sets are also excluded (encard = ⊤); this is equivalent to the Finset version since any infinite equilateral set would contain a (2d+1)-point equilateral subset.

Hypothesis `0 < d` is included (the decomposition notes say d ≥ 1). It is genuinely needed: for d = 0 the space is a single point, the singleton is vacuously equilateral, and 1 > 2·0, so the unrestricted statement is false. This is explained in the theorem docstring.

Only the upper bound (the conjectural half) is the research-open slot. The easy lower bound (the 2d vertices ±eᵢ form an equilateral set of encard exactly 2d) is proved as a `category textbook` companion `exists_isEquilateral_encard_eq`, with supporting `API`/`test` lemmas; this is not an extra slot but documents that the conjectured bound would be sharp.
The related Kusner suggestion for p > 2 (equilateral dimension d+1) is deliberately not formalized, as instructed by the decomposition table.
AMS tags 46 51 52 (functional analysis / geometry / convex and discrete geometry); the given tags were 'geometry, discrete geometry'.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Kusner conjecture

A set of points in a metric space is *equilateral* (or *equidistant*) if any two distinct
points of the set are at the same distance from each other. Let $\ell^1_d$ denote $\mathbb{R}^d$
with the Manhattan ($L^1$) norm $\|x\|_1 = |x_1| + \cdots + |x_d|$. The $2d$ vertices
$\pm e_1, \dots, \pm e_d$ of the cross-polytope form an equilateral set in $\ell^1_d$.

Kusner's conjecture (R. B. Kusner, 1983) states that no larger equilateral set exists:
at most $2d$ points can be equidistant in $\ell^1_d$. Equivalently, the equilateral dimension of
$\ell^1_d$ is exactly $2d$. This is known for $d \le 4$, and the equilateral dimension of
$\ell^1_d$ is known to be $O(d \log d)$ in general.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, Kusner conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kusner_conjecture)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* R. K. Guy, *An olla-podrida of open problems, often oddly posed*,
  Amer. Math. Monthly **90** (1983), 196–200.
* J. Koolen, M. Laurent, A. Schrijver, *Equilateral dimension of the rectilinear space*,
  Des. Codes Cryptogr. **21** (2000), 149–164.
-/

namespace KusnerConjecture

/--
**Kusner's conjecture.** For every $d \ge 1$, at most $2d$ points can be equidistant in
$\ell^1_d$: if $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ is a set such that any two distinct points of $S$ are
at the same $L^1$-distance $r$ from each other, then $|S| \le 2d$.

The restriction $d \ge 1$ excludes the degenerate space $\mathbb{R}^0$, which is a single point.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 46 52]
theorem kusner_conjecture (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) (S : Set (PiLp 1 fun _ : Fin d => ℝ)) (r : ℝ)
    (hS : S.Pairwise fun x y => dist x y = r) : S.encard ≤ 2 * d := by
  sorry

/--
The bound $2d$ in Kusner's conjecture is attained: the $2d$ vertices $\pm e_1, \dots, \pm e_d$
of the cross-polytope are pairwise at $L^1$-distance $2$ from each other.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 46 52]
theorem exists_equilateral_set_encard_eq (d : ℕ) :
    ∃ S : Set (PiLp 1 fun _ : Fin d => ℝ),
      S.encard = 2 * d ∧ S.Pairwise fun x y => dist x y = 2 := by
  let f : Fin d × Bool → PiLp 1 fun _ : Fin d => ℝ :=
    fun p => WithLp.toLp 1 (Pi.single p.1 (if p.2 then (1 : ℝ) else -1))
  have hf : Function.Injective f := by
    rintro ⟨i, b⟩ ⟨j, c⟩ h
    have h' := congrArg (fun x : PiLp 1 fun _ : Fin d => ℝ => (x i, x j)) h
    simp only [f, Pi.single_apply] at h'
    by_cases hij : i = j
    · subst hij
      cases b <;> cases c <;> first | rfl | norm_num at h'
    · simp only [hij, Ne.symm hij] at h'
      cases b <;> norm_num at h'
  refine ⟨Set.range f, ?_, ?_⟩
  · rw [← Set.image_univ, hf.encard_image, Set.encard_univ, ENat.card_eq_coe_fintype_card]
    simp [mul_comm]
  · rintro _ ⟨⟨i, b⟩, rfl⟩ _ ⟨⟨j, c⟩, rfl⟩ hne
    rw [PiLp.dist_eq_sum (by simp)]
    simp only [f, ENNReal.toReal_one, Real.rpow_one, div_one, Real.dist_eq]
    by_cases hij : i = j
    · subst hij
      have hbc : b ≠ c := fun h => hne (by rw [h])
      rw [Finset.sum_eq_single i (fun k _ hk => by simp [hk]) (by simp)]
      cases b <;> cases c <;> first | exact absurd rfl hbc | norm_num
    · rw [← Finset.sum_erase_add _ _ (Finset.mem_univ i),
        ← Finset.sum_erase_add _ _ (Finset.mem_erase.mpr ⟨Ne.symm hij, Finset.mem_univ j⟩)]
      rw [Finset.sum_eq_zero (fun k hk => by
        simp only [Finset.mem_erase] at hk
        simp [hk.1, hk.2.1])]
      rw [Pi.single_eq_of_ne (Ne.symm hij), Pi.single_eq_of_ne hij]
      cases b <;> cases c <;> norm_num

end KusnerConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single slot matches the list-page statement, and the notes' reading (d ≥ 1, common positive ℓ¹-distance, |S| ≤ 2d, p > 2 case excluded) agrees with the article and with Guy (1983)/Koolen–Laurent–Schrijver (2000).
modeling_decisions: Ambient space: ℓ¹_d is modelled as `PiLp 1 (fun _ : Fin d => ℝ)`; its `dist` is provably `∑ i, |x i - y i|` (verified in a scratch example via `PiLp.dist_eq_sum`), so the L¹/Manhattan distance is used with no bespoke norm definition.

Equidistance: `S.Pairwise (fun x y => dist x y = r)` with `r : ℝ` universally quantified. This is equivalent to 'S is λ-equilateral for some λ > 0' from the literature: positivity of r is automatic when S has ≥ 2 points (distinct points have positive distance), and when |S| ≤ 1 the bound |S| ≤ 2d is trivial for d ≥ 1. No `0 < r` hypothesis was added to avoid redundancy.

Cardinality: `Set.encard` (ℕ∞-valued) rather than `Set.ncard` or a `Finset`, so an infinite equilateral set would have encard ⊤ and violate the bound rather than be silently mapped to 0. (Mathematically no infinite equilateral set exists in finite dimension, so this is only a matter of honesty of the encoding.)

Dimension restriction `(hd : 0 < d)`: the table's notes say d ≥ 1. For d = 0 the space ℝ^0 is a single point, so the singleton set has 1 > 2·0 points and the unrestricted statement would be false; I verified this refutation in Lean.
Bound is non-strict `≤ 2 * d`, matching 'at most 2d'. The expression `2 * d` elaborates in ℕ∞ as `2 * (d : ℕ∞)`, which equals `((2 * d : ℕ) : ℕ∞)` (checked by `push_cast`).

Scope: only the ℓ¹ (p = 1) statement is formalized. The p > 2 'equilateral dimension d + 1' suggestion mentioned in the article is not part of the list-page statement and is excluded, as the decomposition table instructs.

An additional `@[category textbook]` theorem `exists_equilateral_set_encard_eq` (fully proved, ~29 lines, no sorry) records that the 2d cross-polytope vertices ±e_i form an equilateral set in ℓ¹_d, i.e. the conjectured bound is attained. It is not a slot; it is included because the article states it and it exercises/tests the PiLp 1 modelling. A reviewer may drop it if they prefer a single-declaration file.
AMS tags `46 52` (functional analysis / normed spaces, and convex & discrete geometry). Category `research open` per the status.
Copyright year 2026, matching the majority of files in the checkout and the latest commit dates.

kusner_conjecture.why: Stated as: for every d with 0 < d, every set S of points of PiLp 1 (fun _ : Fin d => ℝ) (Mathlib's ℓ¹ on ℝ^d) whose distinct points are pairwise at a common distance r satisfies S.encard ≤ 2 * d. Only existing Mathlib primitives are used (PiLp, Set.Pairwise, dist, Set.encard). Checked in a scratch file that dist on this type is ∑ i, |x i - y i| and that the d = 0 instance is refutable (so the 0 < d hypothesis matches the table's 'd ≥ 1').

-/

namespace KusnerConjecture

/--
The Kusner conjecture: for every $d \geq 1$, a set of points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose
pairwise $\ell^1$-distances are all equal to the same positive number has at most $2d$ points.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem kusner_conjecture :
    ∀ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d → ∀ S : Set (Fin d → ℝ),
      (∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧
        ∀ x ∈ S, ∀ y ∈ S, x ≠ y → (∑ i : Fin d, |x i - y i|) = r) →
      S.Finite ∧ S.ncard ≤ 2 * d := by
  sorry

end KusnerConjecture
modeling_decisions: Interpreted the terse list-page phrase “L^1 spaces” using the cited background article as finite-dimensional real coordinate spaces ℝ^d with Manhattan (ℓ¹) distance, for every d ≥ 1.
Represented ℝ^d as `Fin d → ℝ` and wrote the ℓ¹ distance explicitly as `∑ i : Fin d, |x i - y i|`, avoiding the default norm on function spaces, which would not express the intended Manhattan norm.
Expressed equidistance by the existence of one positive real `r` equal to the ℓ¹ distance of every pair of distinct points in the set.

Quantified over arbitrary sets and concluded both `S.Finite` and `S.ncard ≤ 2 * d`; the finiteness conjunct is necessary because `Set.ncard` alone defaults to zero on infinite sets and would not faithfully express “at most 2d points”.
Formalized only the stated upper bound. The cross-polytope lower-bound construction and the related p > 2 conjecture were excluded, as directed by the decomposition.

/-!
# Kusner conjecture

Let $\ell_1^d$ denote $\mathbb{R}^d$ with the $\ell^1$ (Manhattan) norm
$\|x\|_1 = |x_1| + \cdots + |x_d|$. A set $S \subseteq \ell_1^d$ is *equilateral*

The $2d$ vertices $\pm e_i$ of the axis-aligned cross-polytope are pairwise at
$\ell^1$-distance $2$, so the equilateral dimension of $\ell_1^d$ is at least $2d$.
Kusner (1983) conjectured that it is exactly $2d$, i.e. that at most $2d$ points of
$\ell_1^d$ can be equidistant. This is known for $d \le 4$, and an upper bound of
$O(d \log d)$ is known in general (Alon–Pudlák).

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Equilateral dimension](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kusner_conjecture)
- [R. K. Guy, *An olla-podrida of open problems, often oddly posed*,
  Amer. Math. Monthly **90** (1983), 196–199](https://doi.org/10.2307/2975549)

  Geom. Funct. Anal. **13** (2003), 467–482](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00039-003-0418-7)

namespace KusnerConjecture

/-- `ℓ¹[d]` is `ℝ^d` with the `ℓ¹` (Manhattan) norm, so that `dist x y = ∑ i, |x i - y i|`. -/
local notation "ℓ¹[" d "]" => PiLp 1 (fun _ : Fin d => ℝ)

/--
**Kusner conjecture**

At most $2d$ points can be equidistant in $\ell_1^d$: for every $d \ge 1$, if $S$ is a
finite set of points of $\mathbb{R}^d$ such that any two distinct points of $S$ are at the
same $\ell^1$-distance $r$ from each other, then $|S| \le 2d$.

The restriction $d \ge 1$ excludes the degenerate case $d = 0$, where a single point is
an equilateral set of size $1 > 2d$. No positivity assumption on $r$ is needed: if $S$
has two distinct points then automatically $r > 0$, and otherwise $|S| \le 1 \le 2d$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 46 52]
theorem kusner_conjecture (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) (S : Finset ℓ¹[d]) (r : ℝ)
    (hS : (S : Set ℓ¹[d]).Pairwise fun x y => dist x y = r) :
    S.card ≤ 2 * d := by
  sorry

/--
The Kusner conjecture holds for $d \le 4$: the case $d = 3$ is due to
Bandelt, Chepoi and Laurent (1998) and the case $d = 4$ to Koolen, Laurent and
Schrijver (2000).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 46 52]
theorem kusner_conjecture.variants.le_four (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) (hd' : d ≤ 4)
    (S : Finset ℓ¹[d]) (r : ℝ)
    (hS : (S : Set ℓ¹[d]).Pairwise fun x y => dist x y = r) :
    S.card ≤ 2 * d := by
  sorry

/-- Two distinct signed standard basis vectors `± e_i` of `ℓ¹[d]` are at distance `2`. -/
@[category API, AMS 46 52]
private lemma dist_toLp_single {d : ℕ} (i j : Fin d) (a b : ℝ) (ha : |a| = 1) (hb : |b| = 1)
    (h : (i, a) ≠ (j, b)) :
    dist (WithLp.toLp 1 (Pi.single i a) : ℓ¹[d]) (WithLp.toLp 1 (Pi.single j b)) = 2 := by
  rw [PiLp.dist_eq_of_L1]
  simp only [Real.dist_eq]
  by_cases hij : i = j
  · subst hij
    have hab : a ≠ b := fun hab => h (by rw [hab])
    rw [Finset.sum_eq_single_of_mem i (Finset.mem_univ _)]
    · simp only [Pi.single_eq_same]
      rcases (abs_eq zero_le_one).1 ha with rfl | rfl <;>
        rcases (abs_eq zero_le_one).1 hb with rfl | rfl <;>
        first | exact absurd rfl hab | norm_num
    · intro k _ hk
      simp [Pi.single_eq_of_ne hk]
  · rw [Finset.sum_eq_add_of_mem i j (Finset.mem_univ _) (Finset.mem_univ _) hij]
    · simp [Pi.single_eq_of_ne hij, Pi.single_eq_of_ne (Ne.symm hij), ha, hb]
      norm_num
    · intro k _ hk
      simp [Pi.single_eq_of_ne hk.1, Pi.single_eq_of_ne hk.2]

/--
The bound $2d$ in the Kusner conjecture is attained: the $2d$ vertices $\pm e_i$ of the
axis-aligned cross-polytope form an equilateral set in $\ell_1^d$, all pairs of distinct
points being at $\ell^1$-distance $2$.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 46 52]
theorem kusner_conjecture.variants.cross_polytope (d : ℕ) :
    ∃ S : Finset ℓ¹[d], S.card = 2 * d ∧
      (S : Set ℓ¹[d]).Pairwise fun x y => dist x y = 2 := by
  set f : Fin d ⊕ Fin d → ℓ¹[d] :=
    Sum.elim (fun i => WithLp.toLp 1 (Pi.single i 1)) (fun i => WithLp.toLp 1 (Pi.single i (-1)))
    with hf
  have key : ∀ u v, u ≠ v → dist (f u) (f v) = 2 := by
    rintro (i | i) (j | j) huv <;> simp only [hf, Sum.elim_inl, Sum.elim_inr] <;>
      apply dist_toLp_single <;> simp_all <;> norm_num
  have hinj : Function.Injective f := by
    intro u v huv
    by_contra h
    have := key u v h
    rw [huv, dist_self] at this
    norm_num at this
  refine ⟨Finset.univ.map ⟨f, hinj⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [two_mul]
  · rintro x hx y hy hxy
    simp only [Finset.coe_map, Set.mem_image, Finset.coe_univ, Set.mem_univ, true_and] at hx hy
    obtain ⟨u, rfl⟩ := hx
    obtain ⟨v, rfl⟩ := hy
    exact key u v (fun h => hxy (by rw [h]))

end KusnerConjecture

/--
The Kusner conjecture: for every $d \geq 1$, a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ whose distinct
points all have the same positive $\ell^1$-distance has at most $2d$ elements.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem kusner_conjecture :
    ∀ (d : ℕ), 1 ≤ d → ∀ (S : Set (Fin d → ℝ)) (r : ℝ),
      0 < r →
      (∀ x ∈ S, ∀ y ∈ S, x ≠ y → ∑ i, |x i - y i| = r) →
      Cardinal.mk S ≤ 2 * d := by
  sorry
